instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: LegalTech startup providing an AI-powered contract lifecycle management platform for SME legal departments. Automating contract review, clause extraction, obligation tracking, and renewal management. 150 customers across Europe. Expanding into regulatory change monitoring with automated contract impact analysis. We have a dedicated management team across core functions but operate with limited middle management layers. Budget cycles are annual with moderate flexibility for mid-year reallocation if a strong business case is presented. Innovation initiatives compete with day-to-day operational demands for team attention.
answers.pastInitiatives: We experimented with a customer self-service portal two years ago after seeing competitors offer similar functionality. We built an MVP with an external agency in 3 months, but customer adoption was disappointing — only 8% of customers created accounts. We did not invest enough in understanding whether our specific customer base actually wanted self-service before building.
answers.strategicGoals: We are targeting a 20% improvement in operational throughput without increasing headcount. Our processes have grown organically over the years and are overdue for standardization. We suspect that workflow digitization, basic automation, and better data integration between our core systems can unlock significant productivity gains within our current cost structure.
answers.teamSize: We have a small technology team of 8-6 people including developers, a part-time DevOps engineer, and a product manager who also handles project management. The team is fully allocated to maintaining current products and handling integration requests from key clients. Innovation work is done in the margins — there is no formally ring-fenced innovation time or budget.

input.changes_since_last: Acquired 4 new enterprise clients. Expanded into adjacent market. Digital maturity improving.

opportunities.title: Standardize Core Workflow Templates for Enterprise Clients
opportunities.rationale: The primary goal is achieving 20% operational throughput improvement. Standardizing workflows across the new enterprise clients will reduce variability and process friction, making automation feasible and reliable.

first_actions: Map the top three most complex client journeys to identify high-friction manual points (Process Mapping).
Develop standardized templates/playbooks for these core workflows within the internal Knowledge Base.
Pilot the new standardized process with one low-risk, high-volume existing client to gather validation data.
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction of average processing time for the top 3 workflows by 15%
milestones: Completion of process maps for core journeys.
Sign-off on standardized workflow playbooks from leadership/key clients.
Successful pilot completion and measured efficiency gain.

opportunities.title: Automate Internal Data Ingestion and Intake Checks
opportunities.rationale: The prior attempt at customer self-service failed due to poor understanding of need. Instead, focus on internal efficiency: automating the manual data input/validation steps required when onboarding or modifying core client contracts. This frees up valuable team time.

first_actions: Identify 1-2 specific high-volume, repetitive data entry points currently handled manually by staff (e.g., initial client metadata capture).
Develop a basic API/script to ingest and validate this limited data set automatically.
Integrate the script into the existing operational tech stack for testing.
resources_needed: Limited time from DevOps Engineer (for integration)
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction of manual data handling hours per client onboarding by 25%
milestones: Identification and scoping of the first automation target.
Successful deployment into a limited operational environment.

next_steps.action: Host a mandatory 'Process Pain Point' workshop involving key staff and operations to formally map the 3 most time-consuming manual processes.
Present a clear, quantified business case (ROI) for allocating dedicated innovation time/budget to the small leadership team.
Define strict, measurable scope boundaries for the internal automation pilot (Opp 2), ensuring it does not balloon into a full system redesign.

key_weaknesses: Chronic under-resourcing of innovation efforts due to operational demands taking precedence.
Lack of formalized, standardized processes that can scale with the influx of enterprise clients.
Underutilization of internal process automation capabilities (focused too heavily on external customer portals).

improvements: Successful expansion into adjacent markets and acquiring 4 new high-value enterprise clients, validating market fit.
Initial movement toward systematizing processes, demonstrated by the completion of previous opportunities/steps.
persistent_gaps: The organizational culture still views innovation work as a 'side project' rather than an integral part of operational delivery.
Lack of allocated time or dedicated non-billable resources to fully execute process standardization and deep automation.
Data integration remains fragmented across core systems, requiring manual effort.
achieved_milestones: Established key client relationships in the expanded adjacent market.

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: Shifted from a focus on foundational capability building to scaling and standardization. Increased revenue validation through enterprise client acquisition has improved perceived maturity, but structural process gaps remain the primary constraint.
